response.passage: The modern Olympic Games, revived in 1896, are a global celebration of human potential, but they are distinct from the ancient Games held in Olympia, not Athens. The iconic five rings represent the union of five continents, not individual countries. While the Olympics occur every four years, they were cancelled during World Wars, proving they are not held without a break. India’s journey has been inspiring, marked by Abhinav Bindra’s historic individual gold in 2008, which was the first for an independent India. Athletes like Neeraj Chopra have shown brilliance, though he won his gold in Tokyo 2020, not Paris 2024. Success in sports requires strict adherence to fair play. Doping is not limited to injecting steroids; it includes any prohibited method or substance used to gain an unfair advantage. Athletes cannot simply use prescribed medicine without checking if it contains banned substances, as they must follow strict anti-doping protocols. Furthermore, testing is not reserved only for winners; any athlete can be tested at any time to ensure integrity. The Paralympic Games, which began in 1948, are not a 'lower' version of the Olympics but a high-performance competition for athletes with disabilities. India has been winning Paralympic medals since 1972, proving that our success in these games is not a recent phenomenon starting only in 2020.
response.summary: The Olympic and Paralympic movements are global events built on integrity, history, and high-performance standards. India has a long-standing record of success in both events, achieved through dedication and strict adherence to fair play rules.
